answer: An agent marketplace requires each identity to lock a refundable bond before bidding on tasks such as terrace design, dune mapping, or harbor scheduling. The bond stays locked for 30 days after the last job, and verifiable non-delivery triggers forfeiture through escrow arbitration. Creating identities remains easy, but operating a thousand eligible agents requires a thousand bonds, tying up capital and exposing each bond to loss if the attacker takes paid work and fails to deliver.
